Five Circles In Square

GeometryCirclesTriangles
What it shows: Four right triangles inside a square, each with a circle, and one more circle in the middle.
How to play: Drag the dot E around the dashed circle, or focus it and use the arrow keys. Press Make circles equal to see when all five match.
Look for the math

Five circles live in one drawing: one inside each of four right triangles and one inside the little square they leave behind. Move the dot E and every circle changes. Can all five ever be the same size?

Four right triangles

The dot E is kept on the circle that has the left side AD as its diameter, so by Thales' theorem the angle at E is a right angle. The three other dots are just E turned by quarter turns, so all four triangles are the same right triangle: legs a and b, hypotenuse c. Its incircle has radius

r = (a + b − c) / 2

The square in the middle

The four rotated copies of E form a square. When a > b, its side is a − b, so the circle inside it has radius (a − b) / 2. If E goes below the middle, the roles of a and b swap; the drawing still works, only the page's written formula changes sign. The logic test checks both formulas in thousands of positions.

When all five match

Set the two radii equal: (a + b − c)/2 = (a − b)/2. The a terms cancel and c = 2b. That makes a 30–60–90 triangle, with the angle opposite b equal to 30° and the other acute angle 60°. The common radius is c(√3 − 1)/4. The logic test confirms the claim for many square sizes and finds no other angle where the radii are exactly equal; the applet calls it finished when they differ by less than half a pixel.

The live cut-the-knot page now shows a GeoGebra picture instead of the Java applet. A 2012 snapshot embeds the applet named FiveCirclesInSquare, and the explanation above is the page's own. One tiny-canvas quirk is softened here: when E sits almost at the centre of a very small drawing, the applet's line-intersection routine returns a missing centre, while this page keeps the true centre of the square.

Try Make circles equal, then tick Show hint and Show statement to see the lines and angles the applet reveals at that moment.
